data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The distinction between genuine reliability and checklist compliance dissolves if the checklist is explicitly a surface heuristic, in which case compliance IS the mechanism, and the single evaluation only needs to verify that the panel applied the heuristic correctly.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The heuristic loses validity on the evaluation set due to an unanticipated shift, making strict compliance detrimental.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The panel overrides the heuristic based on their own non-expert intuitions, leading to worse-than-checkbook performance.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The problem demands a causal understanding that the surface heuristic cannot provide, making the distinction between structure and proxy critical again.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"If the checklist is not claimed to be a causal model but a validated surface heuristic (e.g., a set of indicators highly correlated with the outcome), then 'mere compliance' is the intended operationalization of reliability. The evaluation distinguishes genuine gain by verifying that the panel adheres to the heuristic strictly and that the heuristic maintains its predictive validity on the evaluation set.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
